title: The keyboard and the notes
summary: Find every note on the keyboard by name, and measure distance in half steps and whole steps. Project: a labelled keyboard map.

practice.question: You want to find C quickly anywhere on the keyboard. Where is it?
options: The white key just left of a group of three black keys
The white key just left of a group of two black keys
The white key just right of a group of two black keys
The first black key in any group
practice.explanation: C sits just left of every group of two black keys. Around the two black keys you get C, D and E. The key just left of the three black keys is F.

practice.question: The music director says "start in Db". Your chart says C#. What do you play?
options: The same black key: C# and Db are two names for it
C# is one key higher than Db
C# is one key lower than Db
practice.explanation: C# is one key above C and Db is one key below D. That is the same black key. Two names for one key are called enharmonic spellings.

practice.question: A chart asks for E#. Which key do you press?
options: The black key between E and F
practice.explanation: Sharp means one key higher. There is no black key between E and F, so one key above E is the white key F. E# and F sound the same.

practice.question: Which pair of notes is a half step apart?
practice.explanation: A half step is the very next key. There is no black key between E and F, so they are a half step apart. C-D, F-G and A-B each skip a black key, so they are whole steps.

practice.question: The choir is singing in G and the leader asks you to take the last chorus up a whole step. What is the new key?
practice.explanation: A whole step is two half steps: G -> G# -> A. The new key is A, and every chord moves up two half steps as well.

practice.question: A soloist says D is too high and asks for it a half step lower. Which key do you move to?
practice.explanation: A half step down is the very next key to the left. From D that is the black key Db, also called C#.

project.title: A labelled keyboard map
checklist: Two octaves of keyboard drawn, with every white and black key labelled
Black keys labelled with both sharp and flat names
Middle C (or the C nearest the centre) marked
Every C and every F on your keyboard played and called out, bottom to top
Ten random notes found in under two seconds each
Half steps played up from C to the next C, all twelve keys
Whole steps played from C (C D E F# G# A# C) and from Db (Db Eb F G A B Db)
A short recording or written log of the half and whole steps you played
